title: Can jazz be taught in school?
summary: Only foundations can be taught; students copying his solos get only a form of expression.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Therefore, how much of jazz do you think can be taught in school ? (inaudible)?

Very little, really. You can teach certain foundations, certain linear things in jazz, that can bring about the helping of a fellow toward him becoming a jazz player. But to actually say "I can teach jazz," it is an impossibility because when you play jazz, you play jazz. You don't fool around with it.
When you said that some of your solos are being used as models to teach youngsters in some of the music schools, it's not possible -- (inaudible) --
That's a form of expression. All that they can get out of what they're hearing is a certain type of form of expression.
But nobody could possibly play what you play.
It comes out you and your experience. (inaudible)

That's right and if it wasn't written down exactly to be played that way the second time, I would never play it that way a second time. But once it has been put down and has been marked as being played that way, I can play it that many times exactly as I so desire. But if I had it my own way, I would play it just a little bit different, each and every time, which is the fruits of being a good jazz player.
